record.paper_title: Modal logics for metric spaces: open problems
record.original_question: Define QMS as an extension of MS that permits variables ranging over positive real or rational distances inside distance operators and quantification over those distance variables. Over metric models, is QMS expressively complete for the two-sorted first-order language with one sort for positive real distances, one sort for points of the underlying metric space, and only two variables allowed for the point sort?

artifact.status_search_result: Searches return the original problem-list source and related work on logics of metric spaces (Kutz, Wolter, Sturm, Zakharyaschev) showing that the variable-free MS corresponds to the two-variable fragment of the first-order distance language over metric spaces, but no source confirming or refuting the expressive completeness of the quantified extension QMS for the two-sorted two-variable fragment was found. The problem appears to remain unresolved in the published literature accessible via search.

status_evidence.title: Logics of metric spaces
status_evidence.snippet: The two-variable fragment of FM is undecidable over metric spaces; MS corresponds to a fragment with the same expressive power as a two-variable fragment in weaker settings.
status_evidence.claim: Background on correspondence between modal language MS and two-variable first-order fragment over metric spaces; no resolution of QMS expressive completeness.

status_evidence.title: From topology to metric: Modal logic and quantification in metric spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses modal and quantified modal logics for metric spaces and their expressivity relative to first-order distance languages.
status_evidence.claim: Closest follow-up work but does not establish expressive completeness of QMS for the two-sorted two-variable fragment.
